# Historical boot schema artifacts

These literal SQL and catalog files were generated by the actual pre-ledger initializers below. Tests reconstruct them without invoking current boot code, verify the reconstructed `sqlite_master` against the historical catalog, and only then run today's initializer. There is no current-initializer/drop-ledger baseline.

| Artifact | Historical Git commit                                            | `packages/boot/src/boot-schema.ts` Git blob | Root `bun.lock` Git blob                   |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| v16      | `dd733fe84cb089072764ce81fa9a030d93c866ef` (master at capture)   | `ce37872fae6b33c162888be9c0e9603c2f3652e8`  | `912d45952e9ded59f4604af372edc3979eada5c1` |
| v18      | `7d476071567c0235fd45dcf158484945e6ab5a44` (PR4 review baseline) | `3f279542f302f7b6a1627ba8a5888e26c5d2e6db`  | `f7a7a14c0a6d844f464617405cb1bdea8003a799` |

Both exports used **Bun 1.4.0 and SQLite 3.51.0** on macOS. Each checkout installed its own frozen dependencies with `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; neither historical tracked tree changed. Only the external export harness was copied into its fixture directory. The harness checks the requested historical version and cannot silently export the current initializer as v16/v18. A second fresh database export from each checkout matched the first export exactly. No user database or credentials were involved.

The exporter, [export-historical-boot-schema.ts](../export-historical-boot-schema.ts), had SHA-256 `533a39f17bcc0b18ad6eed9e81f1fb796823b4665480f59eb416b9241474b352` when executed. Its imports resolve through the historical checkout. The catalog query is exactly `SELECT type,name,tbl_name,sql FROM sqlite_master ORDER BY type,name`. SQL reconstruction omits internal `sqlite_*` objects, which SQLite recreates from the original table declarations; reconstruction tests compare those internal catalog entries too.

## Reproduce deliberately

Run from the comms checkout containing these fixtures, using the recorded Bun version. Use fresh worktree and database paths; do not run the exporter against today's initializer. The commands below show v18; repeat with the pinned v16 commit and version 16.

```sh
fixture_source="$PWD/packages/boot/test/fixtures"
git worktree add --detach /tmp/comms-history-v18 7d476071567c0235fd45dcf158484945e6ab5a44
(cd /tmp/comms-history-v18 && bun install --frozen-lockfile)
cp "$fixture_source/export-historical-boot-schema.ts" /tmp/comms-history-v18/packages/boot/test/fixtures/export-historical-boot-schema.ts
bun /tmp/comms-history-v18/packages/boot/test/fixtures/export-historical-boot-schema.ts /tmp/comms-history-v18-final.db 18 > /tmp/comms-history-v18-final.json
python3 "$fixture_source/boot-schema-history/materialize.py" /tmp/comms-history-v18-final.json "$fixture_source/boot-schema-history"
bunx oxfmt --write "$fixture_source/boot-schema-history/v18.catalog.json"
```

`retained.sql` is separate synthetic, non-secret test data. It is not presented as data exported from an old deployed board. It exercises settings, passkey/session credentials, acknowledged event JSON, the allocator, backups and terminal recovery records against both actual historical schemas. Unfinished recovery is covered separately by the upgrade-refusal tests.

## What the checks establish

Historical v18 adoption preserves the complete catalog except the new boot ledger. Historical v16 upgrades compare against the independently exported v18 catalog: only the known backup provenance additions at rungs 17/18 change the old schema; rung 19 changes protocol metadata only. The tests also retain representative rows and compare file size and SHA-256 across a second initialized, checkpointed and closed process lifetime.

The runtime `verifyBootSchemaShape` probe checks required columns inside the same transaction as ledger adoption. Qualified column names prevent SQLite's double-quoted-string fallback from accepting a missing column. Missing tables/columns must roll back newly stamped receipts and the version mirror. These probes do **not** establish table-versus-view identity, column types, constraints, indexes or validity of existing row values. The independent historical catalog comparisons catch migration-body drift in constraints and indexes; they are test evidence, not a claim of equivalent runtime validation.
